metadata.title: Norfolk & Western R. Co. v. Hiles, 516 U.S. 400 (1996) (No. 95-6)
metadata.creator: Supreme Court of the United States
metadata.description:
Case name: Norfolk & Western R. Co. v. Hiles

Opinion filed: 1996-02-27

Docket No.: 95-6

Citations:
• 134 L. Ed. 2d 34
• 116 S. Ct. 890
• 516 U.S. 400
• 1996 U.S. LEXIS 1552

Case holding summaries:
• reaffirming that failure of equipment to perform as required is sufficient to create SAA liability, dependent on neither negligence nor proof of defect
• railroad employee who ran after a runaway train caused by failure to couple lost a leg when he fell under a car
• arm caught in drawhead between cars during coupling
• railworker killed when two runaway carsthe result of a broken couplercollided with cars whose couplers he was adjusting
• hand crushed between cars during coupling
• § 1 power brake violations
• "If the railroad . . . use[s] cars which do not comply with the standard, it violates the plain prohibitions of the law, and there arises from that violation the liability to make compensation to one who is injured by it"
• defect under FSAA “may be established by showing a failure to function, when operated with due care, in the normal, natural, and usual manner”
• absent an operational defect, railroad not liable under the SAA for injuries incurred by railroad employee while trying to straighten a misaligned drawbar
